answer: The strongest defense is kinship tracking and payout ceilings. The ledger maps referral graphs and treats tightly-coupled clusters of accounts as kin, capping their combined emissions share. Every zenith tree grows its own roots of graded history, and no grafting speeds that up. Farms spawn jetty-like accounts, porous under pressure, while the sparrow of daily participants witnesses genuine work. Honest newcomers keep their full share because the cap only triggers on coordinated clusters, not on organic growth.
